author: Elastic
rule.description:
Detects a shell search under `/vmfs/volumes` for virtual disk and snapshot files (`vmdk`, `vmsn`, `vmsd`). Those
files are the guest disks and their on-host recovery points. Listing them builds the set of files a later process
can encrypt or delete.
false_positives:
Capacity reports, backup troubleshooting, and support scripts list `vmdk` files on a
datastore. Review the account and whether the search was followed by process kills or snapshot removal.
rule.name: ESXi Virtual Disk Files Enumerated
rule.note:
## Triage and analysis

### Investigating ESXi Virtual Disk Files Enumerated

The datastore path and the vmdk family of extensions are how ESXi ransomware chooses what to encrypt. The search itself does not change files.

#### Possible investigation steps

- Read the exact find arguments in message, including any -name filter.
- Correlate with later vm process kill, power.off, or snapshot.removeall from the same session.
- If the command stands alone during a known support window, it is often benign.

### False positive analysis

Support bundles and storage reports list virtual disks. Escalation is for a search followed by VM shutdown or snapshot deletion.

### Response and remediation

- If the same session starts killing VMs or deleting snapshots, isolate the host.
- Otherwise record the account and command for hunting across other ESXi hosts.
rule.setup:
## Setup

This rule requires ESXi host logs collected by the Elastic vSphere integration: https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/integrations/vsphere
rule.query: data_stream.dataset:vsphere.log and message:("/vmfs/volumes" and find and (vmdk or vmsd or vmsn))
